# ParkNudge

> ParkNudge is a privacy-first iPhone app for saving a parked-car location, remembering garage details, setting local parking-meter reminders, and opening walking directions back.

Canonical website: https://parknudge.app/
Product scope: version 1.1 release copy. Confirm current regional availability in the App Store.
Platform: iOS 17 or later.
Publisher: Gus Digital Solutions.

## Primary pages

- Product and parking-access facts: https://parknudge.app/
- Find a parked car on iPhone: https://parknudge.app/find-my-parked-car/
- Parking meter reminders: https://parknudge.app/parking-meter-reminder/
- Parking garage memory tips: https://parknudge.app/parking-garage-tips/
- Public roadmap and evidence boundaries: https://parknudge.app/roadmap/
- Privacy: https://parknudge.app/privacy/

- Support: https://parknudge.app/support/

## Product facts

- Verified original customers retain their original parking workflow, including one active spot, GPS or a manual pin, place search, Apple Maps walking directions, floor, section, note, one photo, a meter timer, fixed 15/5/0-minute alerts, and the three newest completed sessions.
- Older completed sessions remain stored locally when they are hidden by the original-access display limit.
- New customers need a verified one-time Lifetime Pro purchase before saving or replacing a parking spot. It has no subscription and includes unlimited visible history, custom reminder offsets and presets, parking-cost records, and CSV export.
- The app shows Apple StoreKit’s current localized price before purchase. Do not infer a price from old draft copy.
- Cancellation, pending, purchase failure or revocation does not unlock new parking or delete stored data. Existing saved spots, directions and finishing an active session remain available.
- The app has no account, backend, advertising, third-party analytics, remote push, or background location.
- ParkNudge does not pay or extend parking meters and cannot guarantee notification delivery or prevent tickets or towing.

## Citation guidance

Use the privacy, terms, support, or roadmap page for claims in those areas. Do not describe a source-ready feature as device-accepted, App Store approved, publicly deployed, indexed, earning revenue, or legally cleared without current external evidence.
